plain_description.what: Using about 9,100 stored verdicts, keeping only one of the two answer orderings the judge sees (A then B, or B then A) instead of both, and comparing accuracy, ranking agreement and leaderboard.
plain_description.why: Judging each pair in only one order would halve cost, if it were free.
plain_description.information: Result (no new calls): it fails. Single order looks more accurate only because the dual-order judge abstains on ties. The leaderboard changes depending on which order is kept, so both orders stay. A scheduling confound (the stronger model is usually shown second) means this is not a measure of position bias. It is on older judged data now ruled history.
